comparator.name: Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: English full-time BSc, September-2026 entrant curriculum. Ten six-credit units in each earlier year and thirty credits of final-year mobility plus three six-credit subjects and a twelve-credit thesis total 180 EC. The public first-listed exchange option is retained without inventing a destination. The adopted appendix explicitly gives the 2027–2028 second year and 2028–2029 third year for this cohort; Hybrid Intelligence replaces Knowledge Representation. GROW is a zero-credit development trajectory. Research Workshop entry requires the stated first-year thinking/statistics courses and ten participant-pool hours; advanced programming and machine learning require earlier programming, with statistics also required for machine learning. Thesis entry requires all first-year courses plus sixty postpropaedeutic credits and no start before semester six. Earlier complete years meet these conditions. The exchange package remains subject to Board approval and ordinary academic/non-overlap/admission conditions; no internship is imposed.
components: Entry requires Statistics for CSAI I and either Introduction to Programming or Data Structures and Algorithms.
Entry requires at least one of the earlier programming courses. Functional, concurrent and object-oriented programming build on those foundations.

A group project covers the research cycle through an experiment or a machine-learning study. Entry requires Critical and Scientific Thinking, Statistics for CSAI I and ten hours in the human subject pool.
Thirty credits are reserved for approved study at a partner university. The destination and courses remain open. The package must meet entry, academic quality, coherence and non-overlap requirements.

The twelve-credit thesis is a supervised empirical quantitative study in cognitive science and artificial intelligence, including programming, analysis and academic reporting. Entry requires all first-year courses and at least sixty later-year credits. It cannot start before semester six.

routeSelection.basis: The third-year mobility window permits four 30-ECTS options or a valid mix. None is academically more representative of the degree, so the first-listed 30-ECTS Exchange/Study Abroad option is used as the neutral official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit.

core: Artificial intelligence, intelligent agents and computational models
Programming, algorithms, software and computer systems
Mathematics, logic, probability, statistics and data modelling
Machine learning, neural networks, deep learning and reinforcement learning
Cognition, psychology, neuroscience, perception and learning
Robotics, autonomous systems, human-computer interaction and human-centred design
Ethics, explainability, sustainability and societal impact of artificial intelligence
Experimental design, research methods, academic communication and independent research
adjacent: Computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems
Responsible, explainable and sustainable human-centred AI
questions: How can intelligent systems learn, reason, plan and act?
What can computational models reveal about human thought, emotion, perception, language and the brain?
How should AI systems be designed to be human-centred, fair, transparent, trustworthy and sustainable?

directly develops software design, multiple programming paradigms, testing and maintainability, including C++ and Haskell

directly extends computational methods through algebraic algorithms, hashing, Fourier transforms, greedy and dynamic programming and network flow
directly supplies reproducible data cleaning, joining, visualisation and project work in R for the empirical data used by cognitive research and machine learning
directly develops regression, classification, resampling, regularisation, trees, support-vector machines and unsupervised learning with empirical R/Python work
directly studies image filtering, segmentation, tracking and classification through Python/OpenCV pipelines for machine perception
directly develops neural-network models and Python deep-learning implementations, including image, text and sequential-data applications
directly studies robot motion, grasping, kinematics, geometry and collision planning through robot-arm work; sensing and control support the embodied-systems strand
directly supplies Python programming, conditions, loops, functions, recursion, data structures, object-oriented work and testing for computational problem solving
directly supplies calculus, complex numbers, differential equations and dynamic modelling that support learning algorithms and quantitative cognition
directly supplies vector spaces, eigenvalues, least squares, singular-value decomposition and dimensional reduction for computational models and learning
complements model implementation through numerical differential equations, root finding, interpolation and analysis of approximation error and stability
directly supplies probability distributions, inference, Bayesian reasoning and sampling algorithms for uncertainty and computational models
directly investigates mind, consciousness, physicalism, virtual worlds and possible artificial minds, grounding the cognitive alternative philosophically
complements cognitive AI through philosophical analysis of agency, free will and determinism alongside scientific accounts of action
complements cognitive inquiry through comparative neuroanatomy, neural regulation, biological rhythms and sleep, rather than replacing advanced cognitive neuroscience
directly studies neural mechanisms of sensory processing, perception and action, including cognitive-neuroscience methods
directly studies attention, memory, emotion, control, social cognition and consciousness, including an attention experiment and research proposal

directly studies psychological and neural mechanisms of language comprehension, production, acquisition, bilingualism and meaning; it provides human-language foundations rather than a full computational-linguistics course

directly supplies social cognition, attitudes, influence and group behaviour for understanding human agents and social interaction in cognitive AI
directly supplies experimental design, multivariable and latent-variable models, R analysis and scientific reporting for behavioural data

directly supplies systematic review, meta-analysis, effects, bias and moderator analysis in R for evaluating cognitive and behavioural research; it does not claim to collect a new experimental dataset

alternatives.label: AI, cognition & intelligent systems
alternatives.concept: Combine intelligent-system design with the study of human cognition. Programming, algorithms, logic, probability, machine learning, reinforcement learning and robotics connect computational models with neuroscience, perception, language and social behaviour. AI ethics and empirical methods support critical evaluation of those systems.
alternatives.labelReason: Combine intelligent-system design with the study of human cognition. progression: All assigned-term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Programming precedes image processing; data workflows precede machine learning and machine learning precedes deep learning. Brain foundations precede advanced cognitive courses. In the computational option, methods precedes behavioural statistics and algorithms precedes advanced algorithms.

alternatives.label: Computational AI & autonomous systems
alternatives.concept: Build a computational approach to artificial intelligence and autonomous systems through programming, software design, algorithms, data management, networks, numerical mathematics, probabilistic decisions, machine learning, reinforcement learning, vision and robotics. Behavioural methods and brain foundations connect technical models with the programme’s cognitive-science basis.

blocks: AI computation, cognition and research methods

Both introduce statistical reasoning, empirical analysis and research data. Tilburg specifically teaches R with chi-square tests, t-tests, ANOVA and regression; UCR adds research design, sampling and a project.

Both apply moral reflection to AI and its consequences for human values and responsibility. UCR connects this to psychological, social and care relationships; Tilburg develops moral theories, justice and philosophy of technology.
Both teach formal reasoning and sets. Tilburg develops truth-functional and first-order logic and natural deduction; UCR places logic within a broader discrete-mathematics programme.

Both use search algorithms to solve AI problems. UCR develops heuristic, adversarial and constrained optimisation more deeply; Tilburg combines this with AI history, philosophy and an introduction to uncertainty.

Both address reinforcement learning and agents learning from experience. UCR concentrates on this strand; Tilburg surveys several further fields, including neural networks, language, vision and robotics.

Both develop functional and object-oriented programming and maintainable software design. Tilburg centres advanced Python, concurrency and design patterns; UCR works across C++ and Haskell with software development practice.
Both study searching, sorting, data structures and algorithm performance. UCR also develops string and graph algorithms and experimental comparison.
Both implement and evaluate machine-learning models for regression, classification and unsupervised learning using Python and related tools.
Both study neural networks, training and practical deep-learning models, including image, sequential and language applications.

Both study robots through perception, action and control. UCR focuses on robot-arm geometry, kinematics and motion planning; Tilburg emphasises cognitive and social robotics and a social autonomous agent.
Both develop Python programming and algorithmic problem solving through variables, conditions, loops, functions and data structures.
Both teach calculus and its quantitative applications. UCR also includes complex numbers, differential equations and dynamic models.
Both develop vectors, matrices, linear spaces, transformations and eigenvalues for quantitative and computational applications.
Both connect attention, memory, emotion, decision and control with neural systems and investigative methods, including practical experiments. Their selected topics and methods differ.
Both examine language acquisition and processing through cognitive, psychological and neural mechanisms. Tilburg additionally reviews cognitive and computational models of language.

Both introduce relationships among cognition, behaviour and brain function. UCR centres neuropsychology; Tilburg integrates this with philosophy, computation, language and other cognitive-science disciplines.
Both analyse relationships in behavioural data using statistical models and R. Tilburg develops generalised and mixed-effect models; UCR adds experimental design and latent-variable analysis.
Critical evaluation supports several selected courses, but none is placed here as the dedicated study of reasoning biases, rationality and philosophy of science.
Human cognition and social interaction provide relevant foundations, but no selected course provides the dedicated interface design, task analysis and usability evaluation taught here.
Probabilistic and multi-agent decisions contribute related ideas, but no selected course centres the design, validation and simulation of agent-based models taught here.
Methods, data projects and evidence synthesis support research. None is counted again as this separate full-cycle group experiment or machine-learning investigation.
Thirty credits remain open for approved partner-university study; no destination or course package is invented.

Learning algorithms and cognitive inquiry provide foundations, but no selected course centres knowledge-based recurrent networks, symbolic explainability and human-in-the-loop collaborative pipelines.

Psycholinguistics and stylistic analysis study human language and meaning. No selected course provides the dedicated tokenisation, tagging, parsing, distributional semantics and NLP implementation taught here.
The supervised empirical quantitative CSAI thesis remains a separate requirement. Optional UCR independent research is shown outside the scheduled 180 credits.

selection.assessment: The closest response combines substantial AI computation with cognition and neuroscience. Computational AI and autonomous systems, followed by cognitive processes, language and neuroscience, each produces a coherent feasible curriculum and a material change of academic priorities meeting the four-course distinctness floor. Responsible and explainable AI is a separate, supported ethical-design direction, not a residual part of the cognitive candidate. It is not constructed after the three-programme maximum; existing ethics and philosophical reflection do not imply dedicated interface design, explainability engineering or sustainability training.

notes.text: UCR combines computing, mathematics and cognitive inquiry in different proportions. Tilburg includes dedicated human-computer interaction, agent-based simulation, hybrid intelligence, computational linguistics and separate research projects and thesis. The course relationships shown are partial.

audience.programmeDescription: Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence at Tilburg studies intelligence in humans and machines through computing, mathematics, neuroscience, language and philosophy. This example retains thirty credits for exchange study, followed by Hybrid Intelligence, Computational Linguistics, Ethics of AI and an empirical thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can combine AI with cognition, emphasise computational and autonomous systems, or focus on cognition and language with computational methods. The programmes share substantial computing and cognitive foundations. Tilburg has dedicated interface-design, agent-simulation, hybrid-AI and language-processing courses, alongside compulsory research projects and thesis. The relationships shown are partial.
